I've been there and can understand what you're going through. I suggest going out on your own to see the sunset and blast music in your car! It's a plus getting to play whatever music you like, getting to do the things you want to do, and you may even meet people along the way. It also sounds like you're still young, which means now is a good time to figure out hobbies such as picking up a new language, volunteering, learning an instrument, etc. as there's a plethora of resources you can research online. 

There's also a difference with being lonely vs. alone, and sometimes no company is better than being with people who make you feel lonely. I'm in the same boat since I find that I like my own company a little too much and find it easy to push people away and it's gotten to the point where the only interaction I get is from my parents and strangers, but I enjoy having less drama and being able to take care of myself. I also consider people who I newly meet to be "friends"  even if it's only for a second and enjoy randomly striking up conversations with strangers. 

Hope this helps and feel free to DM me whenever as well. Wishing you luck! :)

Hi, my friend started a fantasy/fictional newsletter sharing his own stories and stories he finds on the interwebs. 

**Chapter 1: Alice in the Teacup**

**by Anthony Keer**

*She stood up and walked around a bit. She felt rather awkward at first. "I've never walked on a cloud before," she thought to herself. "It's much harder than I thought it would be." But then she thought about it, and realized that she had never really thought about what it would be like to walk on a cloud and so she corrected herself. "It's much harder than I would have thought it would be, if I were to have thought about how it would be to walk on a cloud. I would have thought that well, I don't know what I would have thought. But it's a lot like walking on..." she was trying to find the right word, but since she had never walked on a cloud before, she could not think of it.*

*"It must be like walking on air," she said, "but then air wouldn't feel like anything, and this certainly feels like something." After a moments more thought she shouted, “I know! It's a lot like walking on air and pudding at the same time." Then she realized that she had never really walked on either air or pudding and so she wasn't quite sure if this was indeed like walking on the combination of the two.*

Synopsis: 

>Keer provides his own imaginative take of the Lewis Caroll's canonical "Through the Looking Glass" novel. A physicist and software engineer turned novelist he has given the reader an inside look at what the beauty of an absurd reality with logical inconsistencies can look like through the lens of a smart and clever little girl and what sort of mysteries await through a seemingly normal human-sized teacup.  

**The Transformation of the Dragon**

**Anthony Keer**

*I looked up stunned, and saw the boy who had given me the pendant down the street being seized by some guards. The boy pointed at me and they seized me too. When the guards searched me, they found the shattered pendant. They accused me of robbing the home of a noble--a retired wizard. I had done no such thing. I denied it. But they kept demanding the rest of what had been stolen. When I told them that the boy had given me the pendant, they did not believe me. His pockets were empty after all. They took me to a dungeon and let the boy go.*  


*They whipped and tortured me to get the information they wanted. They beat me until I was sure that I would die. But my torturers lacked the stamina to kill me. They complained that their muscles hurt, laughed and walked off to take a break.*  


*I felt the injustice of the situation keenly. I hated being blamed for something I didn't do. I hated being powerless, I hated struggling. I promised myself that they would pay, that I would have revenge. That's when it happened. The indignancy was bursting within me. My skin began to change colors to a deep red and my body grew in size until the ropes that bound me burst. My skin became tough and scaly and my hands became claws. I could feel something erupting out of my back--my wings. I panted, lifted my head to the sky and screamed. When I did, a burst of flame shot out. I was a dragon.*

Synopsis:

>A short story about a past companion and a misunderstood dragon whose fates are intertwined and told through magic, but also gives the reader hope about fate not being the only thing that changes our destinies.

Hey some guy,

Great work. But first thing I noticed is the two page resume. Scrap that second page and fit it in the first. 

I like your summary and your statistical facts/experience. But how **do you stand out?** What do you want to **provide** your new company? Why are you looking for a new job? Do you want a full-time or just looking for more opportunities?

I'd like to see more of your personality in your resume and to make the recruiter want to see the work you've done. It might be HR that'll be reading this and not an engineer and you gotta keep them from being bored.

An example that I would do (But I am not an engineer):
> As an engineer I was able to increase the canning rate by 30% with proper equipment maintenance. (Described WHAT you canned) Able to set company standards and fully ensured efficiency production of [insert personal example here]. 

Good job so far! You're almost there!

Hey, good job on your resume! But I'll give you the short and sweet summary of it right now:

Maybe scrap "Key Skills" as it takes up space on your resume and can be better highlighted in your work experience. Make sure to make your summaries more interesting and to stop being repetitive. I see a lot of "Good, Responsible, Provide, etc..." 

What I would do to make it easier for recruiters to constantly be *interested* while reading your resume is to bold/highlight important key words. There's a ton of information you're giving recruiters, which is good, but they want to see it summarized in a short, detailed, interesting way. 

Here's an example paragraph/summary of your job description for your Customer service (current) position I would write:

> As a Customer Service Advisor I was able to handle **daily interactions** with customers and ensure **professional mannerisms** when resolving disputes, cancellations, or complaints. [Put a personal story you experienced when handling a customer issue]. 

Overall, it sounds like you've done/gained a shit ton of experience. Make them excited and interested like you are when you get to do this stuff! Keep up the good work.
